leadIn.title: Lead-In & Context: Will
leadIn.content: Future predictions and sudden decisions: 'The phone is ringing!' — 'Don't worry, I will answer it.' I think tomorrow will be sunnier.

meaningCheck.question: Function check: What is the primary purpose of using Will?
options: To express clear, level-appropriate meaning in structured context
To translate sentences word-for-word from another language
It is an obsolete form never used by native speakers
meaningCheck.explanation: Correct · This structure provides explicit grammatical function and clarity.

meaningCheck.question: Form check: Does correct usage of Will require matching subject, verb, and modifier agreements?
options: No, agreement rules are optional in English
Yes, matching grammatical forms ensures natural, accurate communication
Agreement only matters in formal academic writing
meaningCheck.explanation: Correct · Accurate form and agreement choices prevent misunderstandings.

form.title: Form & Structure: Will
form.content: Subject + will + base verb. Negative: Subject + won't (will not) + base verb. Question: Will + subject + base verb?

pronunciation.title: Pronunciation Notes: Will
pronunciation.content: Spoken stress, weak forms, intonation, and articulation patterns for Will.

controlledPractice.question: Quick decision: 'The phone is ringing : I ___ answer it.'
controlledPractice.explanation: Will is used for decisions made at the moment of speaking.

controlledPractice.question: Which never changes form?
controlledPractice.explanation: Will never takes -s, even with he/she/it: she will come.

controlledPractice.question: Fix: 'I will to help you.'
controlledPractice.explanation: Will is followed directly by the base verb, with no 'to'.
